mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent corporate registry in the jurisdiction of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille Member State): notarization in the origin jurisdiction followed by issuance of a Hague Apostille by the designated Competent Authority; the apostilled original is then submitted to the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the PRC banking institution without further consular legalization. Path B (Non-Member State): notarization in the origin jurisdiction followed by authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of that state and final legalization by the Consular Department of the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that state. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Current Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar of the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille Member State): notarization and apostille by the designated Competent Authority in the origin jurisdiction; acceptable for SAMR and bank KYC without consular legalization. Path B (Non-Member State): notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and Chinese consular legalization in the origin jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and shall not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the WFOE and appointing its legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign shareholder parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille Member State): the executed resolution or power of attorney must be notarized by a local notary and then apostilled by the competent authority of the state of issue. Path B (Non-Member State): after notarization, the document must be authenticated by the foreign ministry of the issuing state and then legalized by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. No sequential chaining of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company through its registered agent or company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille Member State): certified copy notarized locally and apostilled by the designated Competent Authority. Path B (Non-Member State): certified copy notarized locally, authenticated by the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by the Chinese Consulate. The two authentication routes are mutually exclusive and must not be applied cumulatively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Foreign Parent's Principal Clearing Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent's clearing bank or relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille Member State): bank letter signed by an authorized bank officer, notarized, and apostilled by the applicable Competent Authority; accepted for Chinese bank account KYC processes without consular legalization. Path B (Non-Member State): bank letter notarized, authenticated by the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by the Chinese Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, exclusive alternatives and may not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Directors Register Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, registered agent, or corporate service provider of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille Member State): notarization followed by apostille from the competent authority of the state of issue. Path B (Non-Member State): notarization, foreign ministry authentication, and Chinese consular legalization. The authentication path must be selected solely on the basis of the origin state's treaty status and the two paths must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed director, supervisor, legal representative, senior manager, and every Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) with 25% or greater ownership must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, China's domestic sanctions and export-control denial lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list for international banks processing RMB, and local anti-terrorist financing lists required by the People's Bank of China. Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatory for any Politically Exposed Person, and close associates and family members of PEPs must be identified. All negative hits must be escalated to the AML compliance officer and fully resolved before any filing. Ongoing sanctions re-screening must be repeated at least quarterly throughout the life of the WFOE.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration and Pre-Approval System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE statutory name must be in simplified Chinese characters; traditional Chinese, Pinyin-only names, and foreign-language scripts are not accepted as the official legal name. The name must follow the mandatory four-tier statutory structure: (1) administrative division; (2) distinctive trade name, which for a WFOE may be a phonetic or free transliteration of the foreign parent's name; (3) industry or operating characteristics reflecting the principal business, such as remote desktop or information technology; and (4) organization form expressed as 'limited liability company'. The trade name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered enterprise in the same or related industry. Phonetic transliteration is permitted only as the Chinese-character rendering of the foreign parent name, never as a standalone Roman-alphabet name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: China/Chinese (as a leading term without ministerial approval)
Group (unless the applicant qualifies as a group company)
International (without express linkage to a qualifying parent enterprise)
One Belt One Road (without ministerial authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain the written name-verdict notice from SAMR stating the statutory grounds for refusal. The applicant, or the appointed PRC counsel, may file an administrative reconsideration application with the next higher market regulatory authority within 60 calendar days from the date of receipt of the rejection notice. The application must include the original rejection notice, the proposed alternative name structure, and documentary evidence of the foreign parent's trade name. SAMR or the supervising authority must issue a reconsideration decision within 30 working days. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months of the reconsideration decision. During the appeal period, the rejected name cannot be reused in any new application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 6201 remote-desktop software WFOE, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected as the sole registered address by PRC tax authorities, commercial banks, and the State Administration for Market Regulation because a WFOE must maintain a fixed business premises evidenced by a lease agreement, property ownership certificate, rent invoices, and actual or demonstrable operational presence. A serviced office or shared workspace with a physical desk, a proper sublease right, and a formal address agreement may be acceptable for registration and bank account opening, but a P.O. Box or mail-forwarding address is not permissible. Banks will refuse the settlement account, and the tax authority may refuse invoice issuance, where the registered address is a virtual office or commercial mailbox. The WFOE must also display its corporate nameplate at the registered address and remain contactable by municipal inspection teams.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is moderate during the first 12 months: approximately 10-15% likelihood of an unannounced tax inspection if the WFOE applies for VAT general taxpayer status; 20-30% likelihood if the address is a shared office or so-called registered-address-only serviced location; and below 5% for an owner-occupied physical office with ordinary software revenue and full documentary compliance. The municipal tax bureau, SAMR, and public security authorities may jointly inspect abnormal addresses. Required checklist: (1) corporate nameplate at the registered address; (2) lease contract, property ownership certificate, and rent payment invoices; (3) staff presence or demonstrable remote telemetry operations; (4) bank statements and customer contracts; (5) payroll records and tax filings; and (6) a designated contact person present in the inspection city. Failure to pass inspection may result in removal from the market registration register and disqualification for export-oriented tax incentives.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 1 through 45, including Chapter 2 Sections 1 and 2 on establishment, articles of association, and legal representative; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 1 through 13 and 22 through 26; Implementation Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law (2020), Articles 2 through 15; and applicable provisions of the Administrative Regulations on the Registration of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), administered through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration at the registered office location.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application and Integrated Dossier (Enterprise Business License Application).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. For an ordinary Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise engaged in ISIC 6201 remote desktop software and telemetry services, no statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed and no blocked escrow account is required. The registered capital amount is set by the founding shareholder in the Articles of Association and may be denominated in RMB. Contributions may be funded in cash or permissible intellectual property. Any inbound capital contribution received from outside China must be remitted to a foreign exchange capital account opened with a SAFE-designated bank, and subsequent conversion into RMB must be effected under the foreign direct investment capital account compliance rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [WFOE_NAME] LIMITED. The undersigned being all the duly appointed director(s) and the sole founding shareholder representative of [WFOE_NAME] LIMITED (the Company), having waived notice and convening formalities, do hereby constitute and hold the first meeting of the board of directors at the proposed registered office on [DATE] at [TIME]. The meeting is quorate, and each resolution set out below is passed unanimously and shall be effective from the date of registration of the Company. 1. Adoption of Constitutional Documents and Subscription of Share Capital. The board reviewed and approved the final form of the Articles of Association submitted to the State Administration for Market Regulation. The initial registered capital of the Company is [AMOUNT] RMB divided into [NUMBER] ordinary shares with par value of [AMOUNT] RMB per share. The founding shareholder irrevocably subscribes for all such shares and shall pay the subscription amount in cash or in permitted intellectual property in accordance with the contribution schedule set out in the Articles of Association. The board directs the general manager and finance officer to open a foreign exchange capital account with the selected bank, to receive capital remittance, to verify each payment against the approved schedule, and to update the register of members. 2. Adoption of the Registered Office. The board approves as the statutory registered office of the Company the premises located at [REGISTERED ADDRESS] as evidenced by the lease agreement obtained by the Company. The board authorizes the legal representative to execute and file any notice, lease memorandum, change of address filing, or zoning acknowledgment required by the Municipal Market Supervision Administration. 3. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The board appoints [LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE] as executive director, chairperson, and legal representative of the Company. The board appoints [GENERAL MANAGER] as the general manager solely responsible for day-to-day operation. The board appoints [FINANCE OFFICER] to serve as the person accountable for financial, accounting, tax, and foreign-exchange compliance. Each officer accepts the position, and the board authorizes the legal representative to execute all contracts, government filings, and bank instructions. 4. Banking and Payment Mandates. The board authorizes the opening of one basic deposit account, one foreign exchange capital account, and one general settlement account at the designated bank. The finance officer and legal representative shall act as joint signing authorities, with payment limits of [AMOUNT] RMB per transaction. The board authorizes the Company to use the Stripe and Paddle payment rails for software subscription fees received from end users. 5. Further Directions. The board directs the officers to apply for tax registration, social insurance registration, payroll accounts, electronic invoice issuance, foreign investment information filing, and all applicable data-compliant operational contracts, and to report all statutory filings to the next annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Dossier Preparation, Notarization and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Platform, administered by the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory dossier in English and Chinese bilingual format. The sole foreign shareholder, if a corporate entity, must provide its certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, and director register, notarized by a local notary public and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate or apostilled under the HCCH Apostille Convention. Verify that the proposed business scope is not listed on the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Foreign Investment Negative List), as ISIC 6201 software publishing and remote-support services are permitted categories. Submit three proposed Chinese company names and the precise business scope through the SAMR online portal. Ensure the Articles of Association state the registered capital, contribution schedule, governance rules, legal representative mechanism, and liquidation procedure. After the name-reservation acceptance notice is generated, download the electronic acceptance notice and retain it for the establishment filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation and registry status of foreign shareholder
Memorandum and articles of association of the foreign shareholder
Apostilled or consular-legalized shareholder identity documents
Proposed Articles of Association for the WFOE
Name reservation acceptance notice
Lease agreement or registered address certificate
Power of attorney from foreign shareholder to local authorized representative
Board consent and identification of legal representative and supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR rejects or queries the name or dossier, the applicant receives online correction instructions; rectify and resubmit within seven days. If the rejection is substantive, request administrative reconsideration within sixty days or initiate administrative litigation within six months under the Administrative Reconsideration Law and Administrative Litigation Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration through the provincial SAMR Enterprise Registration E-Form System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the foreign-invested enterprise establishment registration e-form using the reserved company name and the pre-approved business scope. Attach the final Articles of Association, shareholder identification documents, legal representative appointment letter, supervisor appointment letter, office lease instrument, and any requisite landlord fire safety documents. All signatures of the overseas shareholder must be made by an authorized attorney-in-fact named in a notarized power of attorney. The registry performs formal and substantive legal review. On approval, SAMR issues the foreign-invested enterprise business license bearing the Unified Social Credit Code, and the Company acquires legal personality. After license issuance, the Company registration record is automatically transmitted to tax and social insurance departments for public records, and the official company seal is engraved by an authorized service provider.
required_dossiers: Completed SAMR foreign-invested enterprise registration application form
Final notarized and legalized Articles of Association
Name reservation acceptance notice
Identity documents of legal representative, executive director, supervisor, and general manager
Office lease contract and property ownership certificate of lessor
Power of attorney and authorization letters
Foreign shareholder corporate resolution approving the establishment
Evidence of lawful funding ability if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If review returns a non-compliance query, use the SAMR electronic correction channel to cure the deficiency within the stated period and resubmit. If the registry fails to issue a decision within the statutory period, file a written complaint with the superior SAMR authority and pursue administrative reconsideration if the application is unlawfully suspended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations for Tax, Social Insurance, Foreign Investment Reporting and Employment Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Office of the State Taxation Administration, Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, Ministry of Commerce Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information System, and SAMR One-Stop Service Window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten days of receiving the business license, complete the integrated post-formation registrations. The SAMR one-stop service will have notified tax and social insurance authorities, but the Company must separately activate tax registration at the district office of the State Taxation Administration, complete social insurance registration and labor contract filing at the local Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and file the foreign investment information report with the Ministry of Commerce through the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information System. Register the statutory registered capital contribution schedule and maintain a shareholder ledger reflecting full foreign ownership. Apply for electronic invoice issuance, determine VAT status as small-scale or general taxpayer, and create payroll and social contribution accounts. All officers must provide identification documents and notarized powers of attorney where applicable.
required_dossiers: Foreign-invested enterprise business license and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Legal representative passport and resident representative identity document
Articles of Association and same registered address certificate
Foreign Investment Information Reporting form
Employment and social insurance registration forms
Tax registration supplemental questionnaire
Lease contract and landlord identification
Notarized company resolution delegating tax and social insurance matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration or social insurance activation is queried, resubmit the missing supporting documentation through the local one-stop window. If the Ministry of Commerce foreign investment filing detects an error, correct and amend the filing within thirty days; late submission penalties are cured by voluntary self-correction before an administrative inspection is commenced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Foreign Exchange Capital Account Registration, Seal Engraving and Operational Go-Live
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAFE-designated commercial bank, local Public Security Bureau-licensed seal engraving service provider, State Taxation Administration invoice platform, and Municipal Market Supervision Administration annual reporting system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a RMB basic deposit account at the selected bank and then apply for opening a foreign exchange capital account with the same SAFE-designated bank. Complete foreign direct investment foreign exchange registration, accept inbound capital remittance, and convert subscribed capital into RMB only for lawful operating purposes within the capital account framework. Obtain the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and invoice special seal from a public-security licensed service provider. Activate electronic invoice quota and the software invoicing platform. File monthly VAT, corporate income tax, and withholding tax returns as they become due. Submit the foreign investor annual report and enterprise annual report to SAMR before each June 30 compliance deadline. For the remote screen-share IoT software product, no separate industrial operating permit is required, but the Company must implement personal information and cross-border data compliance policies before onboarding users.
required_dossiers: Business license original and electronic copy
Articles of Association and establishment resolutions
Legal representative passport and ID
Company seal set including financial and legal representative seals
Basic deposit account registration certificate after bank opening
SAFE foreign exchange registration application and capital contribution schedule
Board resolution designating bank signing officers
Tax registration certificate and expected invoice volume statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE question the capital account application, provide a supplemental board resolution, updated capital contribution schedule, and source-of-funds statement, then escalate through the bank compliance officer. If the annual report or foreign investment report is queried, submit a corrected filing online; if a monetary penalty is proposed, present mitigating evidence and seek lenient first-offender treatment under prevailing administrative grace practices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing site is established; ISIC 6201 remote desktop software publishing and unattended-machine telemetry is a pure digital and consulting activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - the Company does not require a statutory industrial operating permit; the foreign-invested enterprise business license, general tax registration, and electronic invoice authorization constitute the only operating authorizations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - if a future physical facility requires environmental licensing, the competent agency will be the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the provincial Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the current no-pollution software and office activity is Exempt or requires only Environmental Registration; a future industrial change would require a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report for Category A projects or an Environmental Impact Registration Form for qualifying Category B projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No active discharges or emissions arise from remote-screen software operations. If future operations create facilities, the mandatory quantitative limits are the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard GB 8978-1996, the Comprehensive Emission Standard of Air Pollutants GB 16297-1996 with organized and fugitive emission caps, and the Hazardous Waste Storage Pollution Control Standard GB 18597-2001; volatile organic compound limits default to local municipal standards where stricter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial civil-defense fire permits. The registered office must be located in a building that has completed the municipal fire-safety acceptance inspection, with the lessor holding the Fire Protection Acceptance Certificate or equivalent fire-safety filing record. Ongoing workplace safety follows the general Occupational Safety and Health Law applicable to offices, and no special Civil Defense fire permit is required for the pure digital software service activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online enterprise tax portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) available at etax.chinatax.gov.cn and through provincial electronic tax bureau accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the business license issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) is the statutory taxpayer identification number and VAT taxpayer identification number. After SAMR incorporation, the tax registration is automatically synchronized under the multi-license integration regime; the WFOE must activate its tax account through the Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 days after obtaining the business license, authenticate the legal representative and financial officer, complete the taxpayer classification (general or small-scale VAT taxpayer), and formalize invoice issuance capabilities. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment but deriving Chinese-source income is assigned a non-resident taxpayer identification number by the competent STA upon the initial withholding or self-filing procedure; this does not alter the non-resident status of that foreign enterprise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (China does not operate a check-the-box election or a hybrid mismatch election; a Chinese WFOE is mandatorily treated as a Chinese resident enterprise taxed at entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. For VAT purposes only, the enterprise may elect small-scale VAT taxpayer status until annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, after which general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales (mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration threshold; small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment applies below this threshold; VAT registration is required from the effective business license date for any taxable economic activity).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-certified VAT invoice tax-control system or, for fully digitalized e-invoices, through the State Taxation Administration fully digitalized electronic invoice service platform. Invoice data are transmitted in real time to the STA VAT invoice electronic base ledger; each invoice must carry a valid tax-control digital stamp/verification code generated by tax-control equipment or the national e-invoice platform before it can be used for input VAT credit. Monthly VAT filing must reconcile issued invoices, received special VAT invoices, and the electronic invoice ledger, with structured invoice data (OFD/XML) retained for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim 0% VAT export zero-rating for remote desktop access and unattended machine telemetry software services, the WFOE must be a VAT general taxpayer and the supply must qualify as software services or information system services provided to an overseas customer and wholly consumed outside China. The statutory criteria require that the service is supplied to an overseas institution or individual, the customer is not a Chinese taxable entity, the service is not used or performed within China, and the foreign-exchange proceeds are received in accordance with State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) rules. The legal basis includes Caishui [2016] No. 36 and applicable STA announcements on cross-border taxable acts zero-rating; small-scale VAT taxpayers may apply the VAT exemption regime instead of the zero-rating refund regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed cross-border service contract, statement of work, and technical specification evidencing remote screen-share and IoT telemetry software services delivered from China to the overseas customer.
Commercial VAT invoice issued in foreign currency or English, clearly referencing the zero-rated service and the tax rate of 0%.

Bank receipt and foreign exchange income declaration/report issued by the Chinese settlement bank evidencing receipt of the overseas customer's remittance; in China this is the bank-issued Foreign Exchange Receipt Declaration rather than an Inward Remittance Certificate, together with the corresponding SAFE transaction report.

Proof of overseas consumption: customer due diligence records, IP address and geo-location evidence, remote access server logs, unattended machine telemetry endpoint locations, and documentation establishing that no party in China consumes the software service.

If physical goods are exported alongside the software (for example hardware-embedded IoT devices), the Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, export invoice, and export tax-refund declaration filed with the STA export tax-refund system are also mandatory.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and SAFE may audit the zero-rating claim, require full substantiation, and disallow or reverse the 0% VAT treatment and associated input VAT refunds where the documentation is incomplete, fraudulent, or the foreign-exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the required period. Clawback actions include recovery of the short-paid output VAT and refunded input VAT, daily late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day, administrative fines ranging from 50% to 500% of unpaid or underpaid tax and from 100% to 500% of fraudulently obtained export tax refunds, and referral for criminal liability under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China for fraudulent export tax refund or false VAT invoice issuance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime administered by the PBOC and SAFE. Current account items, including software subscriptions, remote support service fees and profit remittances, are broadly convertible once the bank is satisfied that the transaction is genuine, the underlying contract/invoice is present, and tax liabilities are settled. Capital account items are not freely convertible. A foreign investor may inject registered paid-in capital under the FDI framework after completing enterprise establishment and foreign exchange registration, and only through a licensed bank in China; the converted RMB funds from the foreign exchange capital account must be used strictly for the WFOE's operating purposes and may not be channeled into securities investment, entrusted loans, real estate outside business use, or non-business loan repayment. There is no mandatory surrender requirement for export proceeds; retained foreign currency may be held in a current-account foreign exchange deposit. Profit remittance by a WFOE to its non-resident parent is treated as a current-account outward remittance after audited financial statements, enterprise income tax settlement, dividend withholding tax assessment, and a shareholder profit-distribution resolution. The remitting bank will verify the audited financials, tax clearance evidence and corporate authorization; if the WFOE has insufficient foreign currency balances, it may purchase foreign exchange with proper documentation. Practical hurdles include the need for annual statutory audit, local tax clearance, updated beneficial ownership details and a legitimate profit-distribution resolution that matches the paid-in capital account records.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's administration of trade in goods and services, export proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic bank account of the exporting WFOE. Goods export proceeds must be received and reported to SAFE through the bank within 90 days after the export customs declaration, unless a delayed-receipt filing is approved. Service exports, including remote desktop access, IoT telemetry and screen-share software subscriptions, must be collected within the contractual payment date and typically no later than 90 days after invoice issuance or service completion; the bank performs single-transaction verification through the SAFE digital platform. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0%. There is no statutory obligation to convert any portion of export proceeds into CNY; the WFOE may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts in a current-account foreign exchange deposit or voluntarily convert at the commercial rate, provided the underlying transaction is genuine and consistent with tax/customs declarations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury or clearing rail. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully open a corporate foreign exchange capital account for a China-domiciled WFOE, cannot obtain SAFE registration codes for inbound FDI, and cannot act as the settlement bank for statutory capital contributions. Using an offshore EMI as the main treasury account would create a liquidity, verification and AML/CFT gap that Chinese banks and SAFE will not accept. The only acceptable use is as a merchant payment gateway for collecting foreign B2B/B2C SaaS subscription revenues, with settlement routed into a licensed Chinese commercial bank account. Even then, the EMI must operate through a licensed local cross-border payment partner; independent EMI custody of WFOE operating funds is legally barred. Overall viability rating: 2/5 for merchant collection, 1/5 for treasury banking, 0/5 for FDI capital custody.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The WFOE's legal representative, or an authorized signatory holding a valid special power of attorney, must physically attend an in-branch KYC interview at a Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank. Remote consular proxy account opening is not generally accepted as a substitute for the first meeting. If the legal representative is outside China, a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney in Chinese or with certified Chinese translation may allow a resident senior officer to complete account opening; however, the ultimate beneficial owner of the WFOE must still provide video identity verification and pass the bank's pre-MMP and AML screening. Additional statutory directors are not required to appear in-person unless flagged as high-risk beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ubiquitous offshore ownership chain with zero-tax jurisdiction ultimate beneficial owner causing opacity in source of wealth and fund flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passport and permanent-residence proof of the ultimate beneficial owner; residential address verification documentary; 24-month personal bank statements from a regulated foreign bank; source-of-wealth affidavit; certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for each intermediary holding company; register of directors and members; constitutional documents; complete group organogram; written rationale for the offshore conduit structure; and signed AML questionnaires for all entities along the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection remitter name mismatched with the registered foreign shareholder, creating a straw-investor red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 or equivalent payment instruction from the shareholder's regulated bank clearly showing the remitter as the WFOE's registered shareholder; SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration certificate or receipt QR code; board resolution approving the capital contribution; shareholder subscription agreement; audited financial statements of the shareholder; source-of-funds evidence including dividend records, loan agreements or asset disposal contracts; and the final proof that no unrelated third party funded the contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote desktop and IoT telemetry software could be used for unauthorized access, cyber-surveillance or data exfiltration, creating a technology-due-diligence and AML/CFT concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, privacy policy, data-protection impact assessment, product architecture documentation, anti-abuse and multifactor authentication controls, customer acceptance policy, geographic export-control compliance procedures, end-user license agreement, and a technology risk assessment prepared by an independent cybersecurity auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border subscription revenue settled through Stripe or Paddle appears as aggregated payment-platform disbursements instead of direct customer remittances, raising money-transmitter and sub-ledger transparency concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant services agreements with Stripe and Paddle; proof of platform KYC/onboarding; monthly settlement statements; complete customer invoices and receipts; automated accounting sub-ledger linking each settlement to identifiable end customers; IP log or license activation records proving software delivery; chargeback history; and reconciliation reports confirming that no personal accounts are co-mingled.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder routes investment funds via SWIFT MT103 into the WFOE's Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a licensed Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank. The WFOE must first complete SAFE/MOFCOM registration and obtain a banking foreign-exchange establishment/temporary admission code. The remittance must include the exact beneficial-owner name, purpose code for FDI capital contribution, and SAFE registration reference. After the bank effects inward checking and capital registration, the funds may be converted into RMB under bank supervision, credited to a restricted capital-account RMB payment account, and then transferred to the WFOE's ordinary RMB basic deposit account for operating disbursements. A certified public accountant in China then issues a capital verification report confirming the actual paid-in capital received, to be filed with the corporate registry and used for statutory reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For pure software and remote-support trade, the default clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for supplier and subcontractor payments after verification of contract, invoice, tax clearance and purpose-of-payment declaration. For IoT hardware units bundled with software, commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700 and MT720) are accepted for physical-goods settlement, and documentary collections (SWIFT MT400) may be used for smaller trade flows with trusted buyers. All outbound disbursements must be supported by real commercial documentation, must pass bank anti-fraud review, and must be reported to SAFE under the current-account payment verification framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-based RMB/USD forward contracts executed onshore with a licensed Chinese bank based on genuine current-account trade or FDI-related exposure
RMB/USD FX swaps for matching short-term liquidity in both currencies, limited to tenor of up to one year and backed by registered cross-border trade flows
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term shareholder loans or registered foreign debt where both principal and interest are subject to SAFE debt registration

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly prohibited for onshore WFOE treasury; only offshore group treasury entities may use NDFs, and any NDF hedge for the China entity must be nullified by onshore deliverable hedging to avoid violation of SAFE derivatives rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Return through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, integrated with the Foreign Investment Information Annual Report for the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); data shared with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for foreign investment monitoring
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of each calendar year, reporting on data as at 31 December of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file results in inclusion on the Enterprise Operation Abnormality List; failure to rectify within three consecutive years leads to inclusion on the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List, exposing the WFOE to administrative revocation/deregistration, restrictions on directors and legal representatives, enhanced tax and credit investigation, and cross-department joint disciplinary punishment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Return and Final Tax Reconciliation, including related-party transaction disclosure schedules and transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local branch of the State Taxation Administration (SAT) via the Electronic Tax Bureau portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final filing deadline is 31 May of each year for the preceding 12-month business year (1 January to 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a statutory RMB 2,000 administrative penalty, rising to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; overdue tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%; enforcement escalation includes tax lien registration, bank account freezing, seizure and sale of assets, loss of preferential tax treatment, tax credit downgrade, and mandatory restrictions on cross-border payment approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit of the WFOE's complete financial statements by an independent Chinese licensed CPA, producing the audit report and annual financial statements required to support the enterprise annual return and CIT settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and State Taxation Administration (SAT) as part of the audited financial information framework; the signed audit report is retained in the statutory corporate file and presented to shareholders in the annual general meeting cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 May of each year, and in all cases before the enterprise annual return and corporate income tax settlement are submitted; the audit report must be based on the fiscal year ended 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: There is no separate government late fee, but failure to commission and retain an independent audit exposes the WFOE to Company Law and Accounting Law inspection findings, administrative warnings, rejection of the annual return as false or incomplete, ineligibility for tax/credit incentive programs, and persistent default by directors or the legal representative may be treated as grounds for administrative license revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, every Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise is required to prepare annual financial statements at the end of each fiscal year and to have those statements audited by an accounting firm; there is no small-company or zero-revenue exemption, so the statutory baseline threshold is zero. In addition, local tax and foreign investment administrative practice absolutely requires the certified audit file to accompany the annual CIT return and annual information report where any of the following quantitative criteria is present: annual operating turnover exceeding RMB 10,000,000; total assets exceeding RMB 50,000,000; annual average employees exceeding 300; cumulative paid-in foreign capital exceeding USD 5,000,000; or any cross-border related-party transaction, intergroup financing balance, share premium injection, or transfer-pricing item exceeding RMB 5,000,000 in the fiscal year. Applicable accounting standards are the PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), which are largely converged with IFRS; small enterprises may elect the Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but a WFOE with cross-border ownership and software-related service revenue is generally required to apply full CAS reporting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), substantially converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); foreign-invested enterprises report in RMB and present Chinese statutory financial statements audited by an eligible Chinese CPA firm.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO and actual-controller information must be confirmed annually through the joint foreign-investment annual report on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System during 1 January to 30 June. Any shareholding transfer, beneficial owner change, actual controller change, capital contribution change, or share registration amendment must be separately filed with the market regulation authority and reported to the foreign investment information system within 30 days after the change event. The WFOE must update its register of members, board minutes, articles of association, share transfer agreements, and AML beneficial-owner due diligence records concurrently with such reporting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) showing subscribed and paid-in capital, transfer history, call dates, and shareholder identities
Register of Directors and Register of Supervisors
Register of the Legal Representative and corporate minute book containing shareholder resolutions and board resolutions
Register of Charges/Mortgages and pledges over assets or equity interests
Corporate seal usage log and delegated signing authority register
Accounting voucher archive and statutory financial statement file

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualified new integrated circuit/software enterprise may access a two-year exemption followed by a 50% tax reduction for the next three years from the first profitable year; a national high-tech enterprise is taxed at 15%; a small low-profit enterprise is subject to an effective 5% rate (20% statutory rate applied to 25% of taxable income) if annual taxable income does not exceed RMB 3 million, staff not exceeding 300, and total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million; additional 100% super deduction is allowed for qualified R&D expenses; loss carryovers may be extended to 10 years for qualifying high-tech and small low-profit enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A (EIT Annual Return Form A) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (e-Tax/e-bureau)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return Form A must be filed within five months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by May 31 for calendar-year enterprises; quarterly advance EIT returns must be filed within fifteen days after the end of each quarter

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, legal name, unified social credit code, fiscal year, address, and corporate status of the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is the resident taxpayer; non-resident shareholders are not entered on this return. Verify that the overseas parent/shareholder details are disclosed in the related-party transaction disclosure schedule and that the China legal representative is named for service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting total profit (pre-tax profit) determined under PRC Accounting Standards from the audited financial statements, including revenue from remote desktop, screen-share, unattended machine telemetry, and IoT subscription services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize software subscription and telemetry revenue on an accrual basis. Reconcile Stripe/Paddle settlement statements to booked revenue; crypto or offshore payment rail income must be translated to RMB at the central parity rate and fully declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, including dividends from qualified resident enterprises and interest on treasury bonds; any other exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE this box is usually nil. Improperly treating royalties or distribution fees as non-taxable income is a common audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total pre-tax deductions: cost of sales, operating expenses, salaries, cloud hosting, R&D costs, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service and royalty charges are deductible only if supported by contracts, actual services, economic benefit, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; withholding tax on cross-border payments must be evidenced before ensuring deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments increasing taxable income: entertainment expenses above limits, unrelated intercompany payments, excessive royalty deductions, fines, penalties, and non-deductible business gifts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE pays inbound royalties to an overseas related company for screen-share/IoT patented technology, the add-back must be rejected or adjusted unless the payment is at arm's length and the overseas company has real substance and beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments reducing taxable income: R&D super deduction, amortization of software intangibles, qualified donations, and tax-exempt subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a remote software business, the 100% R&D super deduction is critical; keep contemporaneous technical project records, personnel time sheets, and cost accounting to support the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforward: net operating losses previously incurred and carried forward are applied to current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general loss carryforward is 5 years; high-tech and small low-profit enterprises may use 10 years. Confirm the WFOE has not exceeded the carryforward window, especially when losses were accelerated by intercompany transfer pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable enterprise income tax rate and preferential rate: standard 25%, high-tech 15%, or small low-profit effective 5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claims for the software enterprise two-year exemption/three-year half reduction require the WFOE to satisfy software enterprise classification and revenue/R&D personnel ratios; non-resident group revenue cannot be allocated to meet thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable on taxable income: taxable income multiplied by the applicable tax rate minus any tax exemption amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate in RMB on a separate company basis. Inbound intellectual property licensing structured as a cost-sharing or risk-adjusted arrangement can be imputed and taxed if the WFOE lacks control over core functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: foreign tax credit for eligible foreign-source income taxes paid by the WFOE, plus any domestic reinvestment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits must be supported by foreign tax returns and official certificates; credit is limited to the PRC tax on the same foreign-source income. Do not claim credits for taxes paid by a non-resident parent on dividend income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance EIT prepayments and any prior-year overpayments credited against current-year tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Underpaid quarterly installments are subject to daily interest; the annual return finalizes the true liability. If the WFOE has no withholding tax agent status for its non-resident owner, prepayments do not satisfy the separate WHT obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refund due: annual EIT liability less advance payments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund is delayed while the tax office checks related-party pricing and withholding evidence. If tax is payable, payment must be made by the statutory deadline; after May 31 the daily 0.05% late-payment surcharge starts automatically.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return may trigger a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 under the Tax Collection Administration Law; late payment of tax carries a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% (approximately 18.25% annualized); understatement caused by tax evasion is subject to a fine of 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax; serious tax evasion is a criminal offense under Criminal Law article 201 with imprisonment up to seven years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a China resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise receiving the dividend from income derived from China; treaty rate reduction is available (e.g., 5% under the China-Hong Kong DTA if the beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE capital).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner of the dividend. Before making the distribution, the WFOE as withholding agent must file the non-resident enterprise income tax withholding return and, together with the non-resident claimant, submit a treaty relief application to the competent State Taxation Administration office using the forms under SAT Announcement 2015 No. 60. The claimant must provide an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residency state covering the income year, a beneficial ownership self-assessment, constitutional and ownership documentation, board resolutions, background on the business activities, and evidence that the claimant does not simply pass the dividend to a resident of a third country. The competent authority may deny relief if the claimant lacks economic substance, powers over the shares, or substance over form considerations are against the claim. In a cross-application or bilateral mutual agreement procedure, the WFOE may be asked to file protective notices and cooperate with exchange of information requests.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 10% on gross interest received by a non-resident from a China resident enterprise and 10% on gross royalties paid for the use of industrial/commercial/scientific equipment and intellectual property. Under the China-Hong Kong DTA, interest and royalties may be reduced to 7% if the beneficial owner is the Hong Kong recipient; under certain other DTAs the rate may remain 10%, 7% or 6% depending on the counterparty and character of payment. The distinction between software license royalties and remote software services is decisive: payments for a copyrighted software license are royalties, while subscriptions for remote screen-share and IoT telemetry support may arguably be services unless a transfer of rights is evidenced.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File documentation is required if annual related-party transactions reach any of: RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions; Master File is required when total annual related-party transaction value reaches RMB 1 billion; Country-by-Country reporting is required for resident ultimate parent groups with consolidated group revenue of at least RMB 5.5 billion in the previous fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime of the UAE type, but the EIT Law general anti-avoidance rule (article 47 and implementation rules) and the substance requirements of SAT Announcement 2015 No. 60 for treaty benefits allow the tax authority to re-characterize a WFOE that has no recruitment, no local R&D, no board decisions, no operating authority, or no core income-generating activities in Mainland China. The WFOE's remote software and IoT business profits must be economically attributable to personnel, assets and functions located in China; if the Chinese entity is a mere riskless shell, the tax authority may impute profit, deny treaty benefits, disregard the entity, and apply CFC rules to the non-resident parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell entity and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is registered as the nominal contracting entity for remote screen-share/IoT software subscriptions but has no employees, no office, no local management, no technical development, and no decision-making authority; all substantive functions are performed offshore and the WFOE merely accumulates profit to benefit from treaty dividends or to shift group revenue into China at favorable effective rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law article 47, the State Taxation Administration may disregard the entity, re-characterize transactions, and adjust taxable income; under Tax Collection Administration Law article 63 the adjustment may be reclassified as tax evasion with a penalty of 50% to 500% of unpaid tax, plus daily interest and late-payment surcharges; the entity may also be blacklisted in the State Taxation Administration major tax violation case publication system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A Chinese court may pierce the corporate veil under PRC Company Law article 23 and hold shareholders and directors jointly and severally liable when the entity is abused to evade taxes or harm creditors; directors can face travel bans, asset freezes, personal enforcement of restitution orders, and personal criminal liability under Criminal Law article 201 for willful tax evasion, including imprisonment of up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation of intercompany royalties and service fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE enters into related-party technical assistance, trademark, cloud infrastructure, and software license agreements that charge inflated royalties or service fees to erode Chinese taxable income with no actual service performance, no beneficial owner, no comparable transactions, and no Core Income-Generating Activities performed by the offshore payee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law articles 41 and 44 authorize the tax authority to make a re-determination on an arm's length basis, adjust taxable income, and impose interest under article 48; Tax Collection Administration Law article 44 permits collection security measures; the adjustment can be treated as tax evasion and liable to a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; criminal exposure arises under Criminal Law article 201 where false invoices or fictitious agreements are used.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false related-party agreements or knowingly prepare false transfer pricing documentation are liable for civil damages to creditors and the tax authority; the court may order personal restitution from the directors' assets, impose travel bans and blacklisting, and convict them for tax evasion or false issuance of invoices, with imprisonment up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit WHT on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident shareholder/affiliate without withholding the statutory 10% EIT and without obtaining treaty relief, or withholds but fails to remit the amount to the State Taxation Administration within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Collection Administration Law article 69, the withholding agent must pay the amount that should have been withheld and is subject to a fine of 50% to 300% of the unrecovered withholding tax; under article 32, a daily 0.05% late-payment surcharge applies; the unpaid WHT is not time-barred in cases of malicious concealment and interest continues to accrue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, finance officer, and actual controller may be personally liable under the piercing doctrine when the WFOE is left without assets after paying dividends; the tax authority can seize personal assets, terminate export tax refund eligibility, and impose a prohibition on exit; directors who knowingly aided the under-withholding or diversion of tax funds can be prosecuted under Criminal Law article 201 with criminal fines and imprisonment for up to seven years.
